rationale: The text explains a conventional bit-error-rate test setup using a pattern generator, receiver, link, and loopback, but does not identify whether this is a software product, hardware, or a procedure. Non_ai is the best binary choice in the absence of an AI signal, with software scope uncertain.
evidence_spans: A bit error rate test (BERT) typically requires a test pattern generator and a receiver set to the same pattern. They can be used in pairs, with one at either end of a link, or singularly at one end with a loopback at the remote end.
conflict_response: The described generator/receiver/link/loopback setup establishes a conventional communications test procedure, but does not establish a software function or even that the described item is software rather than test equipment or a procedure. I therefore retain non_ai as the best binary choice while weakening it and flagging scope, rather than treating a conventional test setup alone as a supported software-negative.
